# Gold ETF Flows: September 2026
## UK crowned in a record quarter
### Regional and fund-specific analysis of gold holdings and flows in USD.
Gold-backed ETFs and similar products account for a significant part of the gold market, with institutional and individual investors using them to implement many of their investment strategies. Flows in ETFs often highlight short-term and long-term opinions and desires to holding gold.
The data on this page tracks gold held in physical form by open-ended ETFs and other products such as close-end funds, and mutual funds. Most funds included in this list are fully backed by physical gold.
Published: 7 October, 2026

### Highlights
* Global gold ETFs attracted US$10bn in September, lifting Q3 inflows to a record US$31bn, led by European- and North American-listed funds.
* Despite a lower gold price, global holdings rose 67t to a record 4,256t, while total AUM declined 7% m/m to US$574bn.
* UK-listed funds recorded their strongest quarter on record and marginally overtook Chinese-listed funds as the largest source of country-level inflows y-t-d.

### September and Q3 in review
**Global physically-backed gold ETFs** **¹** **attracted US$10bn in September, capping a record quarter in which investors added US$31bn (Chart 1).** All regions recorded inflows during the month, led by Europe and North America. Despite a lower gold price, which contributed to a 7% m/m decline in total assets under management to US$574bn, strong demand lifted global holdings by 67t to a record 4,256t.
During Q3, global gold ETFs’ total AUM rose 9%, while collective holdings grew by 211t. At the country level, the record Q3 inflow was led by the US, followed by an impressive contribution from UK-listed funds. The UK recorded its strongest quarter on record, helping Europe achieve the same milestone at the regional level.
**Chart 1: Western buying drives record quarterly gold ETF inflows**
Global gold ETF flows by region*
Western buying drives record quarterly gold ETF inflows
*As of 30 September 2026.
Source: Bloomberg, Company Filings, World Gold Council

### Regional overview
**North American funds attracted US$4bn in September, taking Q3 inflows to US$12bn.** The US accounted for almost all the region’s monthly inflows, adding US$3.8bn, while Canadian funds attracted a more modest US$206mn. This first quarterly inflow of 2026 marked a sharp reversal from the weakness seen earlier in the year, bringing y-t-d flows firmly into positive territory at US$4.1bn.
September’s inflows came despite a challenging domestic backdrop for gold. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points ² during the month and signalled that further tightening could follow, contributing to upward pressure on Treasury yields and the dollar. These developments increased the opportunity cost of holding gold and weighed on its price.

...

**European gold ETFs saw inflows of US$3.6bn in September, extending Q3 buying to a record US$14bn.** The UK remained the largest contributor, adding US$2.2bn during the month, although buying was relatively broad-based, with funds listed in Germany and France also recording solid inflows. Swiss-listed funds recorded net inflows too, although their holdings declined by 1t, a divergence linked to the mechanics of FX-hedged products.

...

UK-listed funds added US$7.5bn during Q3, their strongest quarter on record, helping Europe to achieve the same milestone at the regional level. Europe also attracted larger inflows than North America, the first time this has occurred in a quarter when both regions recorded inflows since Q2 2021. With US$9.5bn of inflows y-t-d, UK-listed funds have marginally overtaken those in China to become the largest source of country-level inflows in 2026 to date ( **Chart 2** ).
**Asian funds added US$2.3bn in September, marking a third consecutive month of inflows and lifting Q3 inflows to US$4.9bn.** China remained the region’s largest contributor, while India, Japan, South Korea and Singapore also recorded inflows during the month, highlighting the breadth of regional buying.

...

**Gold ETFs listed in other regions attracted US$104mn in September, resulting in a record Q3 total of US$476mn.** Australian funds accounted for virtually all monthly buying, adding US$106mn, which more than offset modest outflows from South Africa. This marked the region’s third consecutive month of inflows.
**Chart 2: UK crowned y-t-d inflow leader**
Cumulative ETF fund flow by selected country*
Chart 2: UK crowned y-t-d inflow leader
*As of 30 September 2026. Countries shown are the five largest contributors to global gold ETF inflows y-t-d.
Source: Bloomberg, Company Filings, World Gold Council

## Gold ETF flows
Data as of 16 October, 2026
Demand captures changes in global/regional gold holdings; fund flows capture the net amount of money (in USD) that comes in or out of gold ETFs globally/regionally. See [methodology note](https://www.gold.org/download/file/16223/ETF-Flows-Data-Methodology.pdf) .

### Volumes hold steady
[**Global gold market volumes**](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/data/gold-trading-volumes) **⁴** **held firm in September, edging down 2% m/m to an average of US$423bn per day.** Activity was mixed across market segments. Over-the-counter (OTC) trading volumes rose 1% m/m to US$229bn per day, supported by LBMA activity, which increased 1% m/m to US$200bn per day.
Exchange-traded volumes slipped 4% m/m to US$187bn per day, driven mainly by an 11% fall in Shanghai Futures Exchange activity, while COMEX trading edged 1% lower. Global gold ETF trading volumes plummeted 19% m/m to US$7bn per day, with declines across all regions.
Positioning data showed a reduction in [**total COMEX net longs**](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/data/gold-open-interest) **, which fell 13% (-100t) over the month to 654t** . ⁵ Managed money fell 84t, reducing net longs to 387t. Other reportables ⁶ also saw their net long positions decline by 16t to 267t into month end.
Meanwhile, net open interest ⁷ in COMEX gold options retreated to levels last seen in early August, although it remained significantly higher than when gold reached its record high in January.
Spreading positions also fell sharply (-156t) in September, reversing a larger build-up in August, with the decline concentrated almost entirely among Other reportables. While this points to a significant reduction in offsetting futures positions, its implications for outright gold prices are less clear.
**Chart 3: Steady OTC trading supports volumes as ETF activity cools**
Average daily trading volumes by segment*
Chart 3: Steady OTC trading supports volumes as ETF activity cools
*Data as of 30 September 2026. Gold price based on the monthly average LBMA Gold Price PM USD.
For more information on trading volumes please visit our Trading Volumes page on Goldhub: [Gold Trading Volume | Gold Daily Volume | World Gold Council.](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/data/gold-trading-volumes)
Source: Bloomberg, Nasdaq, COMEX, ICE Benchmark Administration, Shanghai Gold Exchange, Shanghai Futures Exchange, ETF providers, Multi Commodity Exchange of India, Dubai Gold & Commodities Exchange, Japan Exchange Group, Thailand Futures Exchange, Borsa Istanbul, Bursa Malaysia, Korea Exchange, World Gold Council

## Gold ETFs holdings and flows
*We monitor how fund assets change through time by looking at two key metrics: demand and fund flows.
* Gold ETF demand is the change in gold holdings during a given period. We use this metric to calculate the quarterly demand estimates reported in Gold Demand Trends.
* Fund flows represent the amount of money – reported in US dollars – that investors have put into (or retrieved from) a fund during a given period. For more details, see our [methodology note](https://www.gold.org/download/file/16223/ETF-Flows-Data-Methodology.pdf) .
† 'Global Inflows/positive demand’ refers to the sum of changes of all funds that saw a net increase in holdings over a given period (e.g., month, quarter, etc.). Conversely, ‘global outflows/negative demand’ aggregates changes from funds that saw holdings decline over the same period.

## Gold ETFs holdings

# Meta launches about $35 billion in stock offerings

Meta said on Oct. 26, 2026 that it launched underwritten offerings of about $35 billion: 250 million Series A depositary shares, each a one-twentieth interest in mandatory convertible preferred stock and sized at about $12.5 billion, plus $22.5 billion of Class A shares sold through forward agreements with Morgan Stanley Capital Services and Goldman Sachs.

Meta - Meta Announces Launch of Offering of Depositary Shares Representing Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock and Offering of Class A Common Stock in Connection with Forward Sale Agreements 

### Meta Announces Launch of Offering of Depositary Shares Representing Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock and Offering of Class A Common Stock in Connection with Forward Sale Agreements 

 October 26, 2026 

Supports Meta's continued investment in AI infrastructure and personal superintelligence

MENLO PARK, Calif., Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Meta Platforms, Inc. (Nasdaq: META) ("Meta" or the "Company") announced today the launch of concurrent separate underwritten public offerings of (i) 250,000,000 series A depositary shares ("Depositary Shares") (the "Depositary Shares Offering"), each representing a 1/20th interest in a share of newly issued Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.000006 per share ("Preferred Stock"), and (ii) $22.5 billion of shares of Meta's Class A common stock, par value $0.000006 per share ("Class A Common Stock") offered in connection with the forward sale agreements described below (the "Common Stock Offering" and, together with the Depositary Shares Offering, the "Offerings").

 

Meta expects to grant to the underwriters of the Depositary Shares Offering a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 37,500,000 Depositary Shares, solely to cover over-allotments, if any. Meta intends to use the net proceeds from the Depositary Shares Offering for general corporate purposes. Meta expects to grant the underwriters of the Common Stock Offering a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional $3.375 billion of shares of the Class A Common Stock. If such option is exercised, Meta expects to enter into additional forward sale agreements with each of the forward purchasers (as described below) in respect of the number of shares of the Class A Common Stock that is subject to the exercise of such option. Meta does not expect to initially receive any proceeds from the sale of shares of Class A Common Stock by the forward purchasers (or their affiliates) in the Common Stock Offering. Meta intends to use the net proceeds it receives upon future settlement of the forward sale agreements and any additional forward sale agreements for general corporate purposes.

Financing Plan

These Offerings are part of a financing plan that consists of:

- Concurrent underwritten offerings: Approximately $35 billion of underwritten public offerings, consisting of approximately $22.5 billion of Class A Common Stock and approximately $12.5 billion in Depositary Shares representing Preferred Stock; and
- Future at-the-market offering: The Company plans to launch an approximately $60 billion at-the-market ("ATM") program upon the commencement of trading of the Company's previously announced Class C common stock, par value $0.000006 per share (the "Class C Common Stock"). Press Release
##### October 26, 2026
# SpaceX Secures $40 Billion in the Largest GPU Financing Ever
SpaceX has reached a binding commitment to enter into an approximately $40 billion master finance lease for GPUs and related equipment with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, Inc.
(Apollo).
This lease will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX’s terrestrial compute buildout and is an important step in our plan to build a Super Intelligence future.
It represents the largest committed GPU financing, underscoring the strength of SpaceX’s infrastructure capabilities.
...
The financing has been committed to by a number of financing parties led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, who served as sole structuring agent.
Funds and accounts managed by BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, and capital accounts advised by KKR have also made anchor commitments in the transaction.
Entry into the lease remains subject to certain specified closing conditions and is expected to close prior to year-end 2026, with lease schedules expected to commence upon delivery of GPUs and related equipment in the first half of 2027.

SpaceX Secures $40 Billion in the Largest GPU Financing EverApollo Global Management

##### October 26, 2026 

# SpaceX Secures $40 Billion in the Largest GPU Financing Ever

SpaceX has reached a binding commitment to enter into an approximately $40 billion master finance lease for GPUs and related equipment with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, Inc. (Apollo). This lease will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX’s terrestrial compute buildout and is an important step in our plan to build a Super Intelligence future. It represents the largest committed GPU financing, underscoring the strength of SpaceX’s infrastructure capabilities.

CFO Commentary

“SpaceX aims to deploy the largest compute infrastructure in the world. As demand for compute continues to accelerate, we’re seeing less than one year payback periods on our SI infrastructure investments. This lease diversifies our funding sources and addresses a notable portion of the funding required to deliver on our growth plans as we aim to get additional compute online at record speeds to power Grok for enterprises and consumers, as well as serve existing and future cloud services customers.”

Transaction Details

The financing has been committed to by a number of financing parties led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, who served as sole structuring agent. Funds and accounts managed by BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, and capital accounts advised by KKR have also made anchor commitments in the transaction.

Entry into the lease remains subject to certain specified closing conditions and is expected to close prior to year-end 2026, with lease schedules expected to commence upon delivery of GPUs and related equipment in the first half of 2027.

Additional information regarding the terms of the lease will be available in SpaceX’s Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, also available on the Company’s investor relations website here.

Forward-Looking Statements

This release contains certain “forward-looking” statements, including, but not limited to, statements concerning the timing of the lease closing; our ability to obtain, deploy, and utilize the GPU pods and related equipment; our ability to scale and monetize our SI products, services, and compute infrastructure; the amount, nature, and timing of our capital expenditures; our future debt levels and ability to obtain financing on acceptable terms; and projections of our future financial and operating performance. # Euro slips ahead of central bank meetings, real tumbles 

 By Chibuike Oguh Reuters Updated October 26, 2026 4:50 PM 

 

 U.S. dollar, Euro, Yen, Pound, Turkish Lira, Yuan banknotes are seen in this illustration taken March 24, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration Dado Ruvic Reuters 

NEW YORK, Oct 26 (Reuters) - The euro fell against the dollar on Monday ahead of a busy week of central bank meetings and with crude oil prices remaining elevated, while the Brazilian real tumbled following a surprise election victory by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

The euro was pressured last week as a selloff in French government bonds drove the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the 2011 sovereign debt crisis, reigniting concerns about renewed financial stress across the euro zone.

However, French government bond (OAT) prices rose on Monday after Moody's spared France a credit rating downgrade last week, easing pressure on a government struggling to shore up strained finances.

The euro was down 0.21% against the dollar at $1.1179 but up 0.31% at 176.04 versus the yen.

"The fundamental issue with the euro hasn't changed and spreads have tightened," said Kit Juckes, chief global FX strategist at Societe Generale. "Euro is still vulnerable at this point because the growth outlook isn't good and energy prices are still elevated."

Brent crude futures eased but still held near six-month highs. Elevated oil prices weigh on import-dependent economies such as the euro zone. Brent fell 0.78% to settle at $115.81 per barrel.

The dollar has been supported by resilient US economic indicators, notwithstanding headwinds including rising inflation. The US currency came under selling pressure during a tech-led market selloff last week.

Five major central banks will announce policy decisions later in the week. The US Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan are all expected to hold rates steady despite inflation pressures.

New Zealand's and Canada's central banks are expected to raise rates this week.

The Japanese yen fell 0.43% to 157.46 per dollar. 

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, was up 0.31% at 102. 

"The dollar is doing less well than expected and has some headwinds but US economic data has been pretty resilient," Juckes said.

REAL TUMBLES

The Brazilian real fell sharply against the US dollar after Lula won a historic fourth term on Sunday against Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who is also the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

Bolsonaro led the election's first round but lost in the runoff by over 4 million votes, rattling Brazilian financial markets, which had bet on his victory. He has refused to concede defeat and promised to ask for the result to be annulled.

 Major U.S. stock indexes rose on the first day of a week that will include earnings reports from three Magnificent Seven firms and the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates. 

 The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite, benchmark S&P 500, and blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 0.8%, 0.7%, and 0.3%, respectively. Tech shares got a boost after Anthropic filed its S-1 paperwork, saying it intends to list on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol “ANT.” The Claude maker said it lost $80.7 billion in the six months through June. 

 Stocks fell Friday, with the Dow shedding 650 points, as oil prices continued to climb on threats of escalated fighting in the Middle East. Still, the blue-chip index ended up 0.4% for the week, its third straight weekly gain. The benchmark S&P 500 and tech-focused Nasdaq Composite finished lower over the five sessions.

 The Roundhill “ MAGS” ETF, which tracks the septet, ended up roughly 1%. They closed lower Friday as Microsoft (MSFT) was the only stock in the group to finish the day in positive territory. Tesla (TSLA) shares jumped 5% to pace the group Monday after Barclays upgraded its rating for the stock and lifted its price target. Nvidia (NVDA) added 2.5%. Microsoft shares gained 1.5% amid the news that up to 60,000 employees are eligible for buyout offers. Shares of Meta Platforms (META), which said in a regulatory filing that it intends to raise up to $95 billion in a series of stock offerings to fund its AI ambitions, declined almost 2%. 

 The other big markets story this week is expected to come Wednesday, when the Federal Open Market Committee will announce whether it will stand pat on interest rates. Economists expect the Fed to raise rates at future meetings to combat high inflation, but say there is no rush to raise them for a second consecutive meeting following September’s hike.
